I mave pleasure in presenting this little book to students in the Science of Astrology, with the hope that they will find it useful, instructive, and simple. I must also offer apology for the delay in issuing it; many were the causes that delayed it, the principal being the state of my health, and great pressure of business, consequent on the reprint of my Ephemerises.

It is not perfect, far from it; I, myself, am not perfect, but make as many, or perhaps more, mistakes than many people; but there it is, if you study it earefully, you will need no other book to instruct you in that branch ol Astrology, for I have tuken especial care that it should contain all the essential information necessary for the practice of Horary Astrology. Horary Astrology, unlike its sister Genethliacal, contains many stereotyped rules, to which there is but one interpretation ; rules which mean such a thing, and only that thing; the volume, there- fore, does not possess that originality which characterises tha “ Guides.” What I have aimed at principally is, to amend, correct, and simplify the rules as much as possible. Many of the writers on this subject are far too copious, they give so many different rules, positions, and cou- tingencies, that the young student is utterly bewildered.
